events.title: Best Personal AI Agents in 2026: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Gemini Spark and More, Compared on Memory, Security and Cost
events.summary:
Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Gemini Spark, OpenAI dots, Meta Muse and Perplexity Personal Computer ranked on memory, security defaults and real cost.

The post Best Personal AI Agents in 2026: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Gemini Spark and More, Compared on Memory, Security and Cost appeared first on MarkTechPost.
events.content:
A personal AI agent runs continuously, keeps memory across sessions, and acts inside your apps. You talk to it in a chat app, by email or by voice. It keeps working after you close the window.

The category started small. OpenClaw began in November 2025 as Clawdbot, a weekend project by Peter Steinberger. Twelve months later, Google, OpenAI, Meta and Perplexity all ship their own versions.

The products split into 2 camps. Self-hosted agents run on your machine or server and use any model you choose. Managed agents run on a vendor’s cloud VM and come bundled with a subscription.

How we ranked them

We scored each agent on 3 axes that matter once an agent holds your inbox and credentials.

Memory: what persists, where it is stored, and whether you can read, edit or delete it.

Security: default permissions, the isolation boundary, approval gates, and the public incident record.

Cost: the subscription price, or token spend plus hosting for self-hosted options.

Facts come from vendor documentation, launch posts and independent security research. Prices are US list prices as of November 21, 2026. Ranking reflects overall fit for an individual user, not raw capability.

Comparison table

RankAgentMakerRuns onMemorySecurity defaultStarting costBest for1Hermes AgentNous ResearchYour machine or server; Docker, Modal, Daytona backendsMEMORY.md, USER.md, SQLite FTS5 session search, self-written skillsManual approvals, denied on timeout; hardline denylistFree (MIT) + model tokensDevelopers who want an agent that learns2OpenClawOpenClaw FoundationYour machine or server; opt-in sandboxEditable Markdown workspace files; SQLite sessions since 2.0Full host access unless sandbox is enabledFree (MIT) + tokens; managed hosts ~$12–$49/moWidest chat-channel reach3Gemini SparkGoogleDedicated Google Cloud VMsGoogle account context via connected appsAsks before spending money or sending email$19.99/mo AI Pro (US)Google Workspace users4OpenAI dotsOpenAIOpenAI cloud computer; optional connected computerChats, ChatGPT memory and the dot’s own notesProactive research is read-only; passwords hidden from modelIncluded in eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium plansChatGPT and Codex power users5Meta MuseMetaMuse Secure VM in Meta’s cloudLearns preferences; forgets on requestSentinel agent gates internet access; approvals for email and purchasesFree; $20 and $100 tiersEveryday errands on a free tier6Perplexity Personal ComputerPerplexityYour Mac plus Perplexity cloudNot detailed publiclyOn-device authorization, 2FA, audit trailPro or Max subscriptionMac users who need local files7NanoClaw, IronClaw, ZeroClawOpen-source projectsContainers, WebAssembly or a small Rust binaryVaries by projectIsolation on by defaultFree + tokensSecurity-first self-hosters

1. Hermes Agent (Nous Research)

What it is: Hermes Agent is an open-source agent from Nous Research. 

It runs from a terminal UI, a native desktop app, a local web dashboard and messaging gateways. Parallel counts about 25 supported platforms as of October 2026, including Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Teams and email. Native iMessage arrived in June 2026.

Memory: Memory is the main reason to pick Hermes. It keeps persistent MEMORY.md and USER.md files and curates them with periodic nudges. Session history sits in SQLite with FTS5 full-text search and LLM summarization. Pluggable providers include Honcho user modeling plus 8+ community backends.

Hermes also writes its own skills. It turns completed complex tasks into reusable skills and refines them over time. Skills follow the agentskills.io standard. The /learn command captures a workflow as a slash command without hand-writing SKILL.md.

Security: The docs describe a 7-layer defense-in-depth model. Layers include user allowlists, DM pairing and human approval for destructive commands. Approval mode can be manual, smart (an auxiliary LLM rates risk) or off.

The defaults fail closed. An unanswered approval prompt is denied aft

events.title: Google AI Previews Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API for Large Tool Libraries
events.summary:
Google launched Gemini API Tool Retrieval in preview. Agents keep a large tool library on standby and load each parameter schema only when needed, inside one Interactions API request.

The post Google AI Previews Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API for Large Tool Libraries appeared first on MarkTechPost.
events.content:
Google has launched Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, now in preview in the Interactions API. Gemini API Tool Retrieval lets an agent keep a large tool library available. It does not send every parameter schema in every prompt. The model loads a schema only when a task needs that tool. For agents wired to dozens of functions or MCP servers, it targets a real cost: tool definitions. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension.

TL;DR

Tool: An API feature with no stated tool cap. Google advises static loading under 20 stable tools.

Runs on: Google’s servers (server-side search) or your own registry (client-side). Interactions API, v1beta only.

Performance: Search, schema load and function call resolve in 1 API request in server mode.

Best: 0 extra round trips and no index to host for server-side retrieval.

What is Gemini API Tool Retrieval?

Tool Retrieval is a Gemini API feature that defers tool parameter schemas until the model asks for them. Google’s documentation states the problem plainly. A few dozen function declarations can consume tens of thousands of tokens on every request.

With deferral, the model sees only each tool’s name and a short description. It does not see the parameter schema until retrieval.

How does defer_loading work in the Gemini Interactions API?

You add {"type": "tool_search"} to the tools array. Then you set defer_loading: true on each function to hold back. The @googledevs launch post shows a deferred issue_refund function on gemini-4-hydrogen. Its code comment mentions 50+ other deferred functions.

When the model needs a deferred tool, the response contains 3 steps:

tool_search_call: the model requests a tool by name.

tool_search_result: the API returns the full schema.

function_call: the model emits the call your code executes.

The API resolves the first 2 steps itself. Your app only runs the function_call and returns a function_result.

Deferred functions can carry an optional short_description. It is shown during retrieval and is valid only when defer_loading is true.

Server-side vs client-side retrieval

Server-side is the default. Gemini runs the search, so there is no index to build or host.

Client-side mode uses "execution": "client". Your app runs its own lookup, such as an embedding index, registry or permission filter. It returns matching declarations in function_result.result. Those tools can join mid-conversation, even if absent from the initial tools array. Each client-side search costs 1 extra round trip.

The 2 modes cannot be combined in 1 request. Only 1 tool_search entry is allowed per request.

Does it work with MCP servers and prefix caching?

Yes on both, with caveats. Setting defer_loading: true on an mcp_server entry defers every tool that server exposes. Deferred MCP tools still execute remotely through the Gemini API MCP support.

On caching, deferred schemas stay out of the prompt prefix. Loaded schemas append inline, so implicit caching still applies. The docs add one catch: deferring tools can shrink a prompt below the minimum cacheable size.

What does Tool Retrieval cost?

There is no separate fee. Tokens bill at the model’s standard input, cached and output rates. Each server-side search triggers an extra model call over the full context. Those tokens appear in total_tool_use_tokens, billed at the input rate.

Each loaded schema then stays billed as input for the rest of the conversation. The docs say static loading can cost less for small libraries or per-turn searches.

How does it compare with Claude and OpenAI tool search?

Anthropic and OpenAI already ship similar tool search features, with published savings numbers.

events.content:
史上最大规模IPO在上市次日遭遇剧烈抛售。

人工智能巨头Anthropic（ANT）周五盘中一度大跌15%，最低仅比IPO发行价高出5美分，收盘跌幅收窄至8.5%，报88.91美元，单日市值蒸发约1090亿美元。

这场剧烈震荡浇灭了市场借Anthropic扭转AI板块颓势的预期。周五，英伟达、Meta和甲骨文等AI核心标的随Anthropic同步下挫，令纳斯达克市值蒸发4万亿美元。市场动荡也波及Anthropic的主要竞争对手OpenAI——后者正推进新一轮估值达1.25万亿美元的巨额融资，并急于在明年登陆公开市场。

不过，接近Anthropic及主承销商的人士坚称此次IPO依然成功，强调公司通过IPO及同步售股合计募资超1000亿美元，且在史上最猛烈的市场抛售之一中仍守住发行价上方，周五收盘价较发行价仍高出7%。

配售向老股东倾斜，六成申购机构空手而归
Anthropic上市首日便已显露疲态。

周四中午前，该股以较发行价高出逾30%的价格开盘，但买盘热情迅速消退，全天震荡走低，最终收涨17%。

部分投资者质疑公司与投行对810亿美元IPO股份的配售安排。据知情人士透露，超过一半的IPO股份流向了已持有公司股权的现有投资者，包括Altimeter Capital、Lightspeed Venture Partners和Menlo Ventures。这一比例罕见偏高，反映出Anthropic高管回馈早期支持者的意愿。

其中部分早期支持者为风险投资机构，其原有持股受限于锁定期无法出售。按行业惯例，风投机构通常不会在IPO中获配大量新股，因为这类新股可立即在二级市场出售以锁定收益。此外，知情人士称，Anthropic还将相当比例的IPO股份配售给了Citadel等大型投资机构，引发部分落选投资者猜测公司优先照顾了旗下Claude模型的大客户。

通常情况下，上市公司与投行顾问会仔细甄别申购需求，耗时数日筛选最优股东名册，以确保上市后股价表现稳健、持股结构稳定。但据部分知情人士估算，申请按IPO发行价认购的机构中，约有60%颗粒无收，其中包括大量对冲基金和大型共同基金。另有众多机构仅获部分配售——据《华尔街日报》报道，资管巨头贝莱德提交了约100亿美元的认购申请，最终仅获配约一半。

开盘定价遭质疑，员工即刻套现加剧抛压
除配售争议外，华尔街也在审视发行定价与解禁安排。

一名对冲基金经理质疑，协助决定开盘时机与价格的投行可能将开盘价定得过高，从而制造了难以逆转的下行势能。不过，推迟开盘同样存在风险，股价在此期间可能继续走高。

与此同时，Anthropic的IPO包含一项罕见条款：允许部分在职及前员工立即出售约3亿股股票，按IPO发行价计算价值约260亿美元。在常规IPO中，员工持股通常面临长达数月的锁定期。这部分股份的减持大概率加大了股价下行压力。

与华尔街的焦虑不同，旧金山多名AI从业者表示基本无视了Anthropic股价的回调。

他们周五更关注另一则消息——一位Anthropic数学家宣称，Claude破解了一道困扰人类167年的“千禧年大奖难题”。不少人将其视为AI超越人类智能的信号。此外，这些员工表示，即便按当前股价计算，许多Anthropic员工手中股票的价值仍比本周初高出数百万美元。

AI交易深陷动荡，“绿鞋”已被行使
Anthropic及其顾问深知，在AI交易遭遇迄今最剧烈动荡之际推进上市风险极高，但他们未曾料到会撞上这场“完美风暴”。

过去数周，云计算企业借贷成本上升、英伟达风波的余波，持续加剧市场焦虑。投资者原本寄望Anthropic这位纯AI巨头能够力挽狂澜、重启行情，但这一幕并未发生。

从承销投行的角度看，只要Anthropic股价不跌破IPO发行价，此次上市就仍算成功。然而，一旦破发，投行原本可用于稳价的一项关键工具已然失效。

Anthropic周五上午宣布，此次IPO的“绿鞋”机制（超额配售选择权）已被行使。

“绿鞋”允许承销商向投资者额外配售相当于发行规模15%的股份，承销商随后既可按发行价向公司购入这些股份，也可在股价跌破发行价时从公开市场回购以托举股价。

随着该期权提前行使，后续护盘手段随之减少。此外，12月15日还将有约3亿股Anthropic股票解禁流通，届时该股可能面临进一步抛压。

events.content:
11月20日，国家金融监督管理总局公布批复，同意筹建云南农村商业银行股份有限公司（以下简称云南农商银行）。

这次合并涉及云南省农村信用社联合社（以下简称云南省联社），以及省内122家州（市）、县（市、区）农信法人机构；

按照方案，123家涉改机构将以新设合并方式组建云南农商银行，新银行成立后，将依法承继这些机构的业务、财产、债权债务及其他权利义务。

按云南农信披露的2025年末数据，全省农信系统资产规模超过1.4万亿元，存款和贷款余额合计接近2万亿元，不良贷款余额和不良贷款率已连续六年下降，新银行的注册资本尚未披露。

云南此前曾在部分州市推进统一法人改革。

2022年底，迪庆、怒江两家州级农商银行相继挂牌。2024年11月，德宏州辖内6家农合机构新设合并，组建了一家州级农商银行。普洱、昭通、文山也曾就筹建州市级农商银行，启动清产核资和资产评估服务的采购招标。

2025年11月，云南省联社一行赴内蒙古农村商业银行股份有限公司（以下简称内蒙古农商银行）调研，了解当地改革遇到的难点和应对措施。内蒙古农商银行当年5月挂牌，以新设合并方式一次整合了121家涉改机构，开业时注册资本为580.17亿元。

今年1月5日，云南的省级整合方案通过联合公告对外明确。

公告显示，123家涉改机构已分别履行内部治理程序，通过了新设合并相关决议。整合范围由此前的部分州市，扩大到省联社和全省涉改的州县农信法人机构。

省级农信改革有两种主要做法。

浙江、四川、江苏、江西、贵州等地组建省级农商联合银行，同时保留辖内机构的法人地位。下一级法人设到哪一层，各地也有差别。贵州规划的是一家省级联合银行和9家市（州）农商银行。

内蒙古、甘肃、宁夏等地采用统一法人模式，将纳入整合范围的机构归入同一家省级银行。法人统一后，资本配置和风险管理可以在全省统筹。各地具体怎么合，又有不同安排。

甘肃分两步推进。今年3月，甘肃农村商业银行股份有限公司（以下简称甘肃农商银行）以66家涉改机构为基础新设合并，开业时注册资本为449.19亿元。9月，甘肃农商银行又获批吸收合并24家机构，并将其改建为分支机构。

宁夏由已有的宁夏黄河农村商业银行股份有限公司（以下简称黄河农商银行）直接吸收合并19家县市农商银行。吸收合并批复于6月29日作出、7月7日公布。8月31日，监管部门集中公布这19家机构的解散批复。清产核资后的资产、负债和业务由黄河农商银行承接，原有机构改建为分支机构。

回到云南，联合公告已明确两项安排。

筹建工作小组获授权组织清产核资和资产评估，原股金按各涉改机构审议通过的决议处置。至于原股金具体怎么处置、新银行股东如何构成，现有公告还没有披露。

存量不良资产如何清收处置、云南省联社原有的行业管理职能如何安排，也是筹建阶段待明确的问题。按照批复，筹建工作完成后，工作小组将向云南金融监管局提出开业申请。

events.summary:

经济指标

美国10月PCE物价指数、三季度实际GDP修正、美联储经济状况褐皮书

11月25日，美国将公布10月PCE物价指数。作为美联储最青睐的通胀指标，9月核心PCE同比录得3.1%，目前机构普遍预期10月核心同比或升至3.2%-3.3%。恰逢感恩节假期前夕，该数据还将与美国三季度GDP修正值同步出炉，恐在节前清淡交投中加剧美元与美债波动。

此外，11月25日，美联储将发布最新经济状况褐皮书。作为12月FOMC年内收官议息前的重要参考，报告将汇总12个联储辖区一线调研，聚焦通胀黏性、就业及消费表现，为市场预判利率路径提供关键线索。

中国10月规模以上工业企业利润

11月27日，国家统计局将公布中国10月规模以上工业企业利润同比数据。此前1—9月规上工业利润累计同比大增15.5%（9月单月增14.4%），主要受AI算力等电子行业高景气驱动。

韩国央行决议与11月前20天出口数据

11月26日，韩国央行将召开年度最后一次货币政策会议。受人工智能浪潮带动半导体出口强劲且通胀高于2%目标影响，市场普遍预期该行将加息25个基点至3.25%。

11月23日，韩国将公布11月前20天进出口初步数据。作为全球半导体贸易及芯片行业风向标，韩国11月上旬出口同比暴增111.9%，其中半导体飙升331.2%，且年内累计出口已于11月19日历史性突破1万亿美元。市场将重点关注前20天增速能否延续高位。

日本11月东京CPI

11月27日，日本将公布11月东京CPI数据。作为全国通胀先行指标，市场聚焦核心CPI能否延续10月（同比2.6%）的涨势。受能源补贴退坡与日元偏弱推动，若物价维持高位，将进一步强化日本央行12月加息预期。

财经事件

商务部：中美双方约定在今年11月底前举行下一次人工智能对话 

据新华社，9月20日至23日，中美经贸团队在美国纽约和华盛顿举行经贸磋商，取得积极共识，为两国元首会晤贡献了经贸领域的成果。商务部美大司负责人就有关经贸磋商成果进行解读。 关于中美人工智能对话在本轮磋商中，双方同意，在中美经贸磋商机制下，何立峰副总理与贝森特财长作为中美各自牵头人建立人工智能对话，并进行了首次对话，交流人工智能相关风险和惠益。双方约定在今年11月底前举行下一次对话。双方同意建立人工智能事件的沟通渠道。

 西班牙举行大选 

据新华社，西班牙首相桑切斯5日宣布，将于11月29日提前举行大选。

感恩节、“黑色星期五”购物节，美股全周交易不足4日

11月26日星期四感恩节当天，美股全天休市一日。感恩节次日、11月27日“黑色星期五”购物节，美股于美东13:00提前收市，全周有效交易日不足四天。

 首批18只主动ETF11月23日集体上市 

易方达、汇添富、华安等多家基金公司集中披露旗下主动ETF上市公告书。根据公告，首批18只主动ETF将于11月23日在沪深交易所上市。该批产品此前合计吸金360亿元，平均股票仓位达56.71%，重仓聚焦银行、消费蓝筹及AI算力链。

第二十八届中国高交会

第二十八届中国国际高新技术成果交易会（高交会）将于11月26日至28日在深圳国际会展中心举行。覆盖AI机器人、半导体、低空经济、储能氢能，同期举办深圳科技投资大会。

 OPEC+会议 

OPEC+声明：OPEC+同意在12月维持产量配额不变。 OPEC+小组将于11月29日举行下一次月度会议。

特朗普TRUMP迷因币晚宴 

美国总统特朗普将于当地时间11月22日（北京时间约23日凌晨）在弗吉尼亚州北部的特朗普国家高尔夫俱乐部（Trump National Golf Club Washington, D.C.）出席TRUMP迷因币顶级持有者晚宴并发表主旨演讲。

报道：欧洲央行将讨论将银行最低准备金要求从1%提高至2% 

据路透援引知情人士报道，欧洲央行将于11月25日讨论将银行最低准备金要求从1%提高至2%。

 中国央行：将招标发行2026年第十期和第十一期中央银行票据 

中国央行：2026年11月24日（周二）中国人民银行将通过香港金融管理局债务工具中央结算系统（CMU）债券投标平台，招标发行2026年第十期和第十一期中央银行票据。

巴勒斯坦将于11月28日举行立法委员会选举 

巴勒斯坦总统阿巴斯9日发布总统令，定于今年11月28日举行巴勒斯坦立法委员会选举，而总统选举将于2027年第一季度举行，具体日期另行宣布。

华为Mate X8及全场景新品发布 

华为Mate X8及全场景新品发布会将于2026年11月24日14:30正式举行，旗舰大折叠手机Mate X8将亮相。

财报

美团、小米、B站、理想、戴尔等

下周中概股及港股科技板块将迎来密集财报披露期，美团、小米、哔哩哔哩、理想汽车、戴尔科技等头部企业将陆续放榜。市场将重点聚焦新能源汽车竞争格局下的汽车交付及毛利表现，以及美团与B站的盈利韧性，业绩成色将直接影响板块短期走势。

小米与哔哩哔哩（B站）的2026年Q3电话会均定于11月24日晚间19:30、20:00举行，美团则在11月27日 19:00晚间举行。

events.title: A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels
events.summary:
TensorLean, from Columbia University and CertiK, formally verifies production GPU kernels at the PTX level using Lean. It checked 149 kernel instances, proved 83 correct, and found 38 bugs in FlashAttention, DeepGEMM and more.

The post A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels appeared first on MarkTechPost.
events.content:
Researchers from Columbia University and CertiK have introduced TensorLean, a framework for formal verification of GPU kernels at the PTX level. TensorLean is a Lean-based verifier that proves compiled kernels match a tensor-level math spec. The research team checked 149 kernel instances, including every kernel of FlashAttention-2, -3 and -4 plus DeepGEMM. It proved 83 correct. The remaining 66 led to 38 correctness bugs. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension.

TL;DR

Size: 1.8K-line PTX parser. Specs total 10,278 lines against 151,285 lines of kernel source, a ratio near 15:1.

Runs on: A 16-core workstation. It checks PTX compiled for A100, H100 and B200 kernels.

Performance: 83 of 149 kernel instances proved correct, 38 bugs found across 6 projects.

Best: Caught a FlashAttention-4 data race that never appeared in 17,760 test runs.

What is TensorLean?

TensorLean is a formal verification framework for GPU kernels at the PTX level. 

It starts from unmodified source code. A developer writes a tensor-level spec in Lean. TensorLean then proves 4 properties: no data races, termination, correct output within tolerance, and untouched memory elsewhere.

How does TensorLean verify a GPU kernel?

Specs build on Lean’s Mathlib. Tensor operators follow PyTorch names, so @ means torch.matmul. Each spec has 5 parts: spec_math, spec_mut, spec_layout, spec_tol and requires. The math stays separate from the memory layout.

The pipeline runs in 7 steps:

Start from unmodified source.

Write the tensor-level spec.

Compile to PTX and load a PTX semantics.

Build a happens-before graph to check races and termination.

Symbolically execute to get final memory, identical across schedules.

Lower the spec to PTX-memory level.

Discharge proofs with Lean’s kernel, Z3 and cvc5.

Which techniques make it scale?

Concurrency to sequential: Race-freedom proofs on the happens-before graph cover all CTAs, threads and loop iterations symbolically.

Loop invariants over semirings: Closed forms for tiled, accumulating loops, such as online softmax, need 1 SMT query per loop.

Tolerance proofs: Algebraic error is proved zero. Round-off error is bounded separately, then combined.

Assertions as hints: Developers add tensorlean_assert in source. Each is proved once, then reused.

What bugs did TensorLean find?

The GitHub README lists 38 bugs, all reported upstream. FlashAttention accounts for 23. Liger Kernel has 7, TileOPs 3, TileLang 2, DeepGEMM 2 and Triton 1.

By category, the site reports 19 memory access errors and 13 numerical bugs. It also counts 7 data races, 5 uninitialized memory reads and 5 undefined behaviors. There are 3 algorithm errors, 2 miscompilations and 1 deadlock. One bug can sit in several categories.

Of 102 FlashAttention instances, 56 passed all 4 properties. The other 46 each failed a proof goal on a source bug.

 

How does it compare with other GPU kernel verifiers?

FeatureTensorLeanVoltaProofWrightPTX in Lean (Koska et al.)BuildersColumbia, CertiKMSR India, StanfordNot disclosedSF TensorCode levelPTXPTXCUDAPTXChecks againstLean tensor specReference kernelSafety + equivalenceLean proofsKernels verified149 instances, FA-2/3/4, DeepGEMM, LigerTutorial reductions, SGEMM, FA-style, TileLangKernelBench L1, safety for 74%3 simple kernelsAsync ops (wgmma, TMA)Yes, FA-3 and FA-4Out of scopeNot disclosedYesNew bugs reported38Races, OOB readsNot disclosedNot disclosedCheck time~10 min median, 50 min max0.007 s to ~570 s~3 min per kernelNot disclosed

The key gap versus Volta is configuration coverage. TensorLean says equivalence checkers unroll loops for one concrete setup at a time. It uses symbolic parameters instead.

Key Takeaways

TensorLean proves GPU kernels correct at the PTX level using Lean, Z3 and cvc5.

83 of 149 kernel instances proved correct; 38 bugs found.

23 bugs sit in FlashAttention-2, -3 and -4.

events.title: 为马斯克融资买GPU，高盛“秀操作”
events.summary:
周四，高盛联手阿波罗全球管理公司（Apollo Global Management），协助马斯克旗下的SpaceX完成了约320亿美元债券定价。这批兼具公司债与资产支持证券（ABS）特征的债券，是高盛耗时一年多交出的答卷——试图在不压垮企业资产负债表的前提下，为昂贵的AI芯片找到买单方案。

这笔债券属于SpaceX总额约440亿美元整体融资的核心部分，虽获贝莱德、Pimco等机构认购，但SpaceX为此支付了高昂成本。

本周，市场对AI增长前景的担忧拖累全球市场，美股下跌8.6%。随着支撑全球经济的AI基建不断逼近融资市场极限，这笔高成本交易正被视作其他科技巨头日后采购芯片的潜在范本。

万亿芯片融资的“两难”
给AI芯片融资历来棘手。芯片价格昂贵，使用寿命却只有短短数年。许多采购方不愿发行常规公司债，担心整体债务膨胀、拖累信用评级。

events.content:
周四，高盛联手阿波罗全球管理公司（Apollo Global Management），协助马斯克旗下的SpaceX完成了约320亿美元债券定价。这批兼具公司债与资产支持证券（ABS）特征的债券，是高盛耗时一年多交出的答卷——试图在不压垮企业资产负债表的前提下，为昂贵的AI芯片找到买单方案。

这笔债券属于SpaceX总额约440亿美元整体融资的核心部分，虽获贝莱德、Pimco等机构认购，但SpaceX为此支付了高昂成本。

本周，市场对AI增长前景的担忧拖累全球市场，美股下跌8.6%。随着支撑全球经济的AI基建不断逼近融资市场极限，这笔高成本交易正被视作其他科技巨头日后采购芯片的潜在范本。

万亿芯片融资的“两难”
给AI芯片融资历来棘手。芯片价格昂贵，使用寿命却只有短短数年。许多采购方不愿发行常规公司债，担心整体债务膨胀、拖累信用评级。

借助ABS等复杂工具举债，虽能避免新增债务冲击信用评级，却会带来新问题：ABS市场可能不够大。据Diameter的Goodwin估算，未来市场需采购约1.5万亿美元芯片，其中大部分将依赖债务融资。放眼信贷市场，唯有存量约8.3万亿美元的美国投资级公司债市场具备相近的承接体量。

摩根大通分析师今年6月在报告中写道：“找到合适的芯片融资范式是一个价值十亿美元的问题”，“在某个阶段，需要创造力来匹配AI芯片领域庞大的资金需求，以及五年期久期上相对有限的资本供给”。

跨界结构与“倒置”流程
据知情人士透露，高盛今年夏天向SpaceX抛出了破题方案：由一家特殊目的载体（SPV）采购英伟达芯片并发行债券，再通过与这家火箭、卫星及AI公司签订的约五年期租约还本付息。这套架构本质上是ABS，但债券保留了常规公司债的部分特征，包括配有美国证券统一识别码（CUSIP），从而吸引到专注高等级公司债的投资者。

相比此前支持Anthropic算力扩张的350亿美元融资项目“Big Sky”，高盛还把资金流程“倒了过来”。Big Sky通过私募配售让投资者承诺出资，等设备到位后再分批提款，债券随后才转为可供更广泛机构交易的格式。这种分阶段做法增加了复杂度，初期也限制了交易，对习惯随时买卖的公司债买家并不友好。

高盛给SpaceX的方案要求投资者预先全额出资。芯片交付前，资金先存入专用账户，可配置美国短期国债等短期工具，以产生的收益对冲设备就位前的融资成本。待GPU陆续交付，账户再放款采购并出租给SpaceX。债券一经发行，合格机构投资者即可直接交易，不必等待分批提款。

机构买单，但溢价高昂
SpaceX这笔整体融资总规模约440亿美元，包含优先和次级部分。据知情人士透露，整体买方覆盖保险公司、结构化信贷买家、资产管理机构及养老基金。在周四定价的约320亿美元债券中，约60亿美元于本周完成了银团分销。

SpaceX披露，交易支持方包括贝莱德、KKR和高盛资产管理。知情人士称，太平洋投资管理公司（Pimco）认购了约40亿美元，Blue Owl也是基石投资者之一。

不过，为了吸引买盘，SpaceX付出了高额溢价。本周向公司债买家发售的证券，定价较SpaceX今年早些时候发行的同期限债券高出约100个基点；而这批旧债近期在二级市场的跌幅持续扩大，已令债券交易员感到震惊。

events.title: NVIDIA Releases Alpamayo 2 Edge: A 2B Reasoning VLA for DRIVE Thor
events.summary:
NVIDIA released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2B-class reasoning vision-language-action model that plans driving trajectories and explains them on DRIVE AGX Thor, at 160 to 190 ms pixel-to-trajectory latency.

The post NVIDIA Releases Alpamayo 2 Edge: A 2B Reasoning VLA for DRIVE Thor appeared first on MarkTechPost.
events.content:
NVIDIA has released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a compact reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) model for autonomous driving. Alpamayo 2 Edge is a 2B-parameter model that plans trajectories and explains them inside the vehicle. It targets NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor, not a datacenter GPU. The goal: reasoning-based planning within onboard compute and latency budgets. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension.

TL;DR

Size: 2B-class. Card breakdown: 2.45B backbone + 0.2B action expert (HF metadata says 3B). Context length: not disclosed (measured prompt: 3,236 tokens).

Runs on: NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor with the FP8 + TensorRT Edge-LLM recipe. BF16 PyTorch needs 16 GB+ GPU memory, validated on 1x H100 80GB.

Performance: Strong closed-loop driver for its size; mid-pack on reasoning QA.

Best: 15.15 km per at-fault incident in AlpaSim, about 60x Qwen-Drive-1.0 4B (0.25 km).

Worst: nuReasoning numeric score of 48.67; LingoQA 75.2 trails Alpamayo 2 Super (79.2).

Bottom line: Best: reasoning-based planning at 160 to 190 ms on in-car hardware. Worst: only H100 validated, and real-time Thor speed needs the FP8 recipe.

What is Alpamayo 2 Edge?

Alpamayo 2 Edge is an open NVIDIA VLA model that turns surround-camera video into a 6.4-second plan. It is the in-car member of the Alpamayo family, next to the 34B cloud model Alpamayo 2 Super.

Per the model card, the 2.45B backbone pairs a 1.96B language model with a 0.41B SigLIP2 encoder. A 0.2B diffusion action expert sits on top. The backbone comes from NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge and is Nemotron-based. NVIDIA markets the model as 2B, while Hugging Face metadata shows 3B.

What goes in and what comes out?

For trajectory prediction, the model reads 6 cameras and 22 frames per observation. The 2 front cameras give 5 frames each, the other 4 give 3 each. It also takes a navigation instruction and 20 historical ego poses.

Output is 64 waypoints from 0.1 to 6.4 seconds. The action expert predicts acceleration and curvature, then a unicycle model integrates them. The text output is a Chain-of-Causation (CoC) reasoning trace. The model also answers free-form questions about a driving scene.

How does adaptive reasoning work?

During routine driving, the model emits special <NOMINAL> tokens instead of a full reasoning trace. It writes CoC reasoning only when a scene needs it. Fewer tokens means less compute per planning step.

How was Alpamayo 2 Edge trained?

NVIDIA team lists these ingredients:

Offline distillation from CoC autolabels generated by Alpamayo 2 Super.

About 115,000 hours of multi-camera driving video and about 3.7M CoC traces.

Closed-loop RL post-training in AlpaGym, learning from its own actions in simulation.

Multi-resolution inputs for cheaper encoding of surround views.

How fast does it run on DRIVE AGX Thor?

Hugging Face weights ship in BF16 and run as a PyTorch model. Real-time use on Thor needs the Alpamayo Developer Hub recipe. It stages the checkpoint and the DFlash2 drafter, then calibrates FP8 scales. Next it exports ONNX graphs and builds TensorRT engines with TensorRT Edge-LLM plugins.

NVIDIA reports 160 ms to 190 ms pixel-to-trajectory latency, depending on how much the model reasons. The reference setup is DRIVE AGX Thor-X with DRIVE OS 7.2.7.0, CUDA 13.4 and TensorRT 11.3.1.9. In NVIDIA’s demo video, PyTorch BF16 plans at 0.76 Hz. The optimized FP8 Thor pipeline plans at 13.02 Hz in AlpaSim. Partner Embedl says it reached 10 Hz on AGX Thor in under 48 hours.

On a workstation GPU, the card recommends at least 16 GB of memory. NVIDIA measured 12.06 GiB peak process memory on 1 H100 with 6 trajectory candidates. Other GPU architectures are not yet validated.

How does Alpamayo 2 Edge score on benchmarks?

NVIDIA compares Edge with Alibaba’s 4B Qwen-Drive-1.0. In AlpaSim closed-loop driving, Edge covers 15.15 km between at-fault incidents versus 0.25 km. That is about 60x. Open-loop minADE is 0.53 m versus 1.68 m.

events.title: 韩国“救市”！准备启动股市稳定基金，或为2008年来首次，放宽公司回购限额3个月
events.summary:
韩国政府宣布启动股市稳定基金激活准备工作，并同步出台多项市场稳定措施，这是2008年全球金融危机以来该基金第三次面临实际动用的可能。此举背景是全球AI产业情绪持续恶化，韩国股市遭受重挫。

上述措施出台的直接导火索，是KOSPI指数20日单日暴跌逾5%，美国纳斯达克指数同日下挫5.28%。与会官员判断，全球AI产业生态系统面临政策风险上升、AI盈利及融资前景不确定、美国数据中心监管收紧、半导体出口管制加码等多重压力，市场担忧情绪持续蔓延。与此同时，外资持续净流出，企业回购力度趋于减弱，市场缺乏有效承接力量，"卖出韩国"压力显著加剧。

events.content:
韩国政府宣布启动股市稳定基金激活准备工作，并同步出台多项市场稳定措施，这是2008年全球金融危机以来该基金第三次面临实际动用的可能。此举背景是全球AI产业情绪持续恶化，韩国股市遭受重挫。

韩国副总理兼财政部长Lee Hyoung-il于22日主持召开金融市场紧急会议（F4会议），宣布上述措施。会议决定，政府将立即启动股市稳定基金（증안펀드）激活机制的准备工作，视市场情况随时部署。与此同时，上市公司自股回购每日申报量上限将自24日起放宽三个月，并同步启动为期三个月的非法卖空专项监控期。

上述措施出台的直接导火索，是KOSPI指数20日单日暴跌逾5%，美国纳斯达克指数同日下挫5.28%。与会官员判断，全球AI产业生态系统面临政策风险上升、AI盈利及融资前景不确定、美国数据中心监管收紧、半导体出口管制加码等多重压力，市场担忧情绪持续蔓延。与此同时，外资持续净流出，企业回购力度趋于减弱，市场缺乏有效承接力量，"卖出韩国"压力显著加剧。

维稳基金：2008年后首次进入激活准备状态

股市稳定基金是韩国用于填补国内股票市场流动性缺口的政策工具。该基金上一次实际动用是在2008年11月，彼时韩国交易所等机构在全球金融危机期间于当年10月筹设规模5,150亿韩元的基金，自11月起按月入市，持续至2009年3月。此后，该基金在2020年和2022年两度进入准备状态，但均未实际入市。

此次为2008年后首次启动激活准备工作。政府表示，将立即审查基金激活机制，确保可依据市场状况迅速部署，同时研究提升基金运作效能的配套措施。

与会官员强调，尽管近期市场波动加剧，但AI产业中长期成长预期的合理性仍获广泛认可，不应过度恐慌或踩踏式抛售。

回购松绑与卖空监控双管齐下

在市场稳定措施层面，政府宣布自24日起，未来三个月放宽上市公司自有股票回购的每日申报量上限。韩国此前对企业回购设有较严格的数量限制，每日申报量不得超过计划回购总量的10%与过去一个月日均成交量25%两者中的较大值，同时不得超过公司总股本的1%。

此次松绑旨在扩大企业回购操作空间，增强市场下跌时的买方承接力量。近期，企业回购一直是吸纳外资抛售的重要力量，但随着大型企业回购计划临近尾声，市场对承接力量减弱的担忧升温。

针对非法卖空，金融监督院（FSS）与韩国交易所将联合运营三个月的专项强化监控期，对发现的违规行为严格处置。

此外，政府还将密切跟踪信用贷款、保证金交易及强制平仓动向，防止连锁抛售压力扩散引发市场进一步动荡，并强化强制平仓预告等投资者保护措施同步推进。

"卖出韩国"压力持续，外资流出创纪录

据路透报道，韩国股市正深陷"Sell Korea"困境。外资净流出已连续数月延伸，累计净流出规模创LSEG数据记录新高，市场承压的根本症结在于买盘持续萎缩。

尽管三星电子（Samsung Electronics）、SK海力士（SK Hynix）等AI芯片核心企业盈利屡创新高，并推出规模庞大的股东回报计划，但市场走势与企业基本面之间的背离持续扩大。分析人士指出，市场走势当前更多受制于买盘匮乏，而非企业基本面的恶化。

Kiwoom证券分析师Han Jiyoung表示："我们基本上正在经历全面的'卖出韩国'趋势。市场当前面临的挑战，是寻找能够吸引外资回流的催化剂。"

在此背景下，政府推出上述一揽子救市措施，释放出托底市场的明确信号。官员同时强调，AI产业中长期基本面并未发生根本性变化，当前的恐慌情绪存在过度之嫌。

events.title: Has AI solved the Riemann hypothesis? Claim makes waves at 200th birthday event in China

events.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
events.summary:
A new real-world test puts AI coding agents in a simulated developer job with colleagues, project boards, and incomplete handoffs, where they have to keep developing software on their own and reliably close open tickets in a messy daily workflow. Even Opus 5.5 and Astra fall far short, solving fewer than one in ten tasks completely. The models finish clear, standalone assignments quickly, but they lose track as autonomous developers.

events.title: Nintendo’s Switch 2 console is $50 off for Black Friday
events.summary: Those hoping to save some cash on a Nintendo Switch 2 can do so starting today, November 22nd, through Saturday, December 5th, giving you plenty of time to think about it after Cyber Monday has passed. For a limited time, Nintendo has knocked $50 off one of its two current console bundles, temporarily rolling back […]
events.content:
Those hoping to save some cash on a Nintendo Switch 2 can do so starting today, November 22nd, through Saturday, December 5th, giving you plenty of time to think about it after Cyber Monday has passed. For a limited time, Nintendo has knocked $50 off one of its two current console bundles, temporarily rolling back the $50 price increase that went into effect in early September.

It’s tough to predict which bundle will be most popular for your household. The Mario Kart World bundle runs $499.99 (previously $549.99) and includes the console, a digital copy of the aforementioned game, and three months of Nintendo Switch Online. Then there’s the Nintendo Switch Sports Resort bundle for $529.99 (price unchanged for Black Friday), which includes the more recent minigame-filled title instead. Both are currently available from Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Nintendo.

Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle

Where to Buy: $549.99 $499.99 at Amazon $549.99 $499 at Walmart $549.99 $499.99 at Best Buy
Nintendo has delivered hit after hit since the console launched in mid-2025. There are now plenty of excellent games to justify snagging a Switch 2, including, most recently, the stellar remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Plus, the newer console can play nearly all of the original Switch games, and it’s wirelessly compatible with the older system’s Joy-Con and Switch Pro controllers.

If you’re planning to get a Switch 2, below are some useful guides filled with accessory recommendations. From tempered glass screen protectors and protective cases to controllers, there are plenty of goodies that’ll help you take better care of your Switch 2 and get more enjoyment from it.

But while the Charmera's usefulness stopped at snapping grainy photos and terrible videos, the Kodak SlideTag goes one step […]
events.content:
After expanding its Charmera collection with a Millennium Edition featuring Y2K-inspired designs earlier this year, Reto's follow-up to its tiny Kodak camera is an equally small digital photo frame you can use to display your shots. But while the Charmera's usefulness stopped at snapping grainy photos and terrible videos, the Kodak SlideTag goes one step further. It also functions as a Bluetooth tracker that's compatible with either Apple's Find My or Google's Find Hub tracking networks.

The Kodak SlideTag will be available for $34.99 each and, like the Charmera, will feature a series of retro designs distributed in mystery boxes so you don …
